key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon-steel components exposed to corrosion and sliding wear.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spraying.
Vary spraying parameters and examine droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate corrosion and wear behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher coating porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates with increasing humidity.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear results involve Si3N4 counterface balls and may not generalize to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
